Interactively Edit a SEM Graph

Source: R/shiny-graph_editor.R
graph_editor.Rd

Launch a Shiny editor for an existing sem_graph object. Drag nodes, adjust node dimensions and labels, change edge connections and curvature, edit supported plotting aesthetics, and change graph-level plotting settings. For multigroup or multilevel graphs, switch between panels. Optionally synchronize node positions across groups within the same level. Changes are shown in a ggplot preview and can be undone, redone, or reset.

Usage

graph_editor(graph)

Arguments

graph

An object inheriting from class sem_graph, typically created by prepare_graph().

Value

An edited sem_graph object when Done is clicked, or NULL when Cancel is clicked. The supplied object is not modified in place.

Details

This function requires the optional packages shiny and htmltools. They are checked at runtime and do not need to be installed for other tidySEM functionality. The editor uses update_graph() to maintain node geometry without rerunning layout or edge-routing algorithms.

Panel switching does not change the underlying graph. When enabled, Apply layout to all groups copies node positions (not aesthetics, dimensions, or edge properties) to same-named nodes in other groups at the same level. This setting is available only for multigroup models.

Edits are saved automatically within the app. Clicking Done returns the edited graph; clicking Cancel returns NULL.

See also

prepare_graph(), update_graph()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  # graph is an existing sem_graph object
  graph <- prepare_graph(
  edges = data.frame(from = "x", to = "y"),
  layout = matrix(c("x", "y")))
  edited <- graph_editor(graph)
  if (!is.null(edited)) plot(edited)
} # }
